title: The Last Scholarship
premise: Isandro Brightwater has spent four years at Hollow Creek High keeping his head down, counting the days until graduation frees him from a town of nine hundred that never let him forget he's different. When his history teacher pairs him with Theo Vance—his former best friend turned tormentor—for a semester-long local history project, Isandro expects misery. Instead, digging through the town archives, they uncover a buried scandal involving Theo's family and the scholarship that built the school, forcing both boys to choose between loyalty to what they were and truth about who they're becoming. As their uneasy partnership deepens into something neither can name, Isandro must decide whether telling the whole truth is worth losing Theo right before prom—and learns that belonging was never something he had to wait for.
about_author: Felix Thornbury grew up in a small mountain town where everyone knew everyone's business, an experience he now mines for fiction. He writes stories about kids who refuse to stay invisible.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Ways to Be Seen
chapters.summary: Isandro narrates his survival strategy at Hollow Creek High: keep quiet, keep moving, count the days. A hallway incident reminds him why invisibility matters. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Assignment Board
chapters.summary: Mr. Okafor announces the semester-long Local Legacies project and reads pairings aloud. Isandro Brightwater and Theo Vance. The class goes silent; Theo's jaw tightens. POV: Isandro. Beat: dread and disbelief.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo corners Isandro to negotiate rules: minimal contact, split work, no talking about eighth grade. Isandro agrees but notices cracks in Theo's armor. Beat: brittle hostility hiding old wounds.

chapters.title: Archive Basement
chapters.summary: First research session in the county archive basement. Dust, microfiche, awkward proximity. They find a 1974 photo of the school's founding benefactor, Aldous Vance—Theo's great-grandfather. Beat: reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: What Eighth Grade Did
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Isandro and Theo as inseparable friends until Isandro came out and Theo, terrified of his own family, pulled away and joined the mockery. Beat: grief for a friendship that died quietly.

chapters.title: The Scholarship File
chapters.summary: They discover the Vance Scholarship funded half the town's school—and that its founding documents reference a sealed 'incident' from 1975. Theo wants to stop digging. Beat: first shared secret.

chapters.title: Dinner at the Diner
chapters.summary: Forced to interview townsfolk, they work the Blue Plate Diner together. Old-timer Ruthie mentions 'the girl who left in '75.' Theo goes pale. Beat: unease turning into compulsion.

chapters.title: Locker Note
chapters.summary: Someone slips a note into Isandro's locker: 'Stay away from the Vances.' He assumes it's a prank but keeps it. Beat: paranoia sharpening his sense of being watched.

chapters.title: Garage Bandage
chapters.summary: Isandro sees bruises on Theo's arm during a work session. Theo deflects. Isandro recognizes the flinch—he's seen it in mirrors. Beat: reluctant empathy cracking old resentment.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Porch
chapters.summary: Ruthie tells them about Marisol Reyes, a scholarship student who vanished from town records in 1975 after accusing Aldous Vance of something. Beat: the past becomes personal.

chapters.title: Split Decision
chapters.summary: Theo demands they drop Marisol and pivot to 'safe' topics. Isandro refuses—the project is his one shot at a real future beyond this town. First real fight. Beat: stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: Home Front
chapters.summary: POV shift: Theo at home, his father's temper, his mother's silence, the weight of the Vance name. He understands exactly what Marisol faced. Beat: guilt he can't outrun.

chapters.title: Truce Over Fries
chapters.summary: A late-night diner session; cold fries, warmer conversation. They agree to continue secretly, splitting findings. Something almost like friendship flickers. Beat: cautious thaw.

chapters.title: The Sealed Box
chapters.summary: In the archive's restricted section they find a box marked with a court seal. The clerk warns them off. Theo photographs the label anyway. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: School subplot: prom approaches, and Isandro wants to bring a date—a boy. Rumors ripple through nine hundred people fast. Beat: visibility has a price.

chapters.title: Caught Reading
chapters.summary: Theo's father discovers the photocopied archive pages in Theo's backpack. A violent confrontation. Theo shows up at Isandro's window that night, shaking. Beat: trust forged in crisis.

chapters.title: Floorboards and Confessions
chapters.summary: Theo sleeps on Isandro's floor. In the dark, he admits things he's never said aloud—not everything, but enough. Isandro holds the silence like something fragile. Beat: intimacy without a name.

chapters.title: Marisol Found
chapters.summary: Online sleuthing locates Marisol Reyes, alive, seventy miles away, a retired teacher. She agrees to talk—if they come alone. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Road Trip
chapters.summary: They skip a Saturday to visit Marisol. Her account: Aldous exploited scholarship students, and the town buried it to protect its money. Beat: righteous anger and vertigo.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Marisol asks the hard question: 'Will you tell it, or will you protect them like everyone did?' Both boys leave unable to answer. Beat: theme made explicit—loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Someone reports their archive trespassing. Mr. Okafor suspends their project access pending review. Theo suspects his father; Isandro wonders if Theo folded. Beat: trust tested.

chapters.title: Hallway Confrontation
chapters.summary: Theo publicly snaps at a jock mocking Isandro, outing himself as Isandro's defender. Whispers ignite. Isandro didn't ask for rescue and resents the cost. Beat: friction between pride and gratitude.

chapters.title: Mother's Album
chapters.summary: Isandro's mom reveals she knew about the '75 rumors her whole life and chose silence to keep their grocery store afloat. Isandro sees how deep the rot goes. Beat: disillusionment with everyone he loves.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Working late in the archive, close in the lamplight, they nearly kiss. Theo pulls back, terrified. Neither speaks of it. Beat: ache of almost.

chapters.title: Cold Shoulder Week
chapters.summary: Theo withdraws completely, avoiding Isandro at school and home. Isandro throws himself into finishing the project solo. Beat: heartbreak disguised as productivity.

chapters.title: Okafor's Office
chapters.summary: Mr. Okafor, revealing he once tried to teach this history and was run out of it, offers them a choice: safe project or true one—but the true one means going public. Beat: mentor moment, agency returned.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Isandro finds a 1975 letter in digitized court records: Marisol's sworn testimony, suppressed by the school board—including signatures of current town elders. Beat: the smoking gun.

chapters.title: Threats
chapters.summary: Anonymous messages escalate; someone keys Isandro's car. His parents, scared, urge him to drop it. For the first time, he refuses them. Beat: courage hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Theo's Choice
chapters.summary: Theo confronts his father with the letter. The fallout is brutal—he's told to leave if he sides with 'that boy.' He packs a bag. Beat: loyalty inverted; truth chosen at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Two Boys, One Doorstep
chapters.summary: Theo arrives at Isandro's door with his bag and the original letter he took from his father's study. They plan how to make the town listen. Beat: alliance becomes love, finally said plainly.

chapters.title: Going Public
chapters.summary: They present their findings to Mr. Okafor and the school board: the suppressed testimony, the scholarship's poisoned origins. The room erupts. Beat: climax begins—truth detonated.

chapters.title: Backlash
chapters.summary: The town splits. The diner boycotts Isandro's family's store. Theo's father threatens legal action. Prom is 'postponed indefinitely' by a panicked board. Beat: darkest hour.

chapters.title: Marisol Returns
chapters.summary: Marisol comes to town unannounced and speaks at an emergency community meeting, face to face with the descendants of those who silenced her. Beat: witness as weapon; catharsis.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: The school board, shamed and split, votes to rename the scholarship and formally acknowledge the record. It isn't everything, but it's real. Beat: imperfect victory earned.

chapters.title: Prom, Rescheduled
chapters.summary: Students organize their own prom when the board stalls. Isandro is asked to help plan—and decides to go openly, with Theo. Beat: reclaiming joy as defiance.

chapters.title: Before the Gym Doors
chapters.summary: Prom night. Isandro waits outside the gym, terrified, hand in Theo's. Inside: stares, then Ruthie leading a slow clap, then music. Beat: vulnerability rewarded; belonging claimed.

chapters.title: Slow Song
chapters.summary: On the dance floor, they talk about after—different colleges, different cities, whether this survives June. No easy promises, only honest ones. Beat: bittersweet tenderness.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Caps thrown, names read. Isandro receives the renamed Reyes-Vance Scholarship for his project. The town that watched him disappear watches him stand. Beat: full-circle triumph.

chapters.title: Last Drive Out
chapters.summary: Isandro and Theo drive the edge-of-town road one last time before summer scatters them. They don't say goodbye. Beat: release without erasure.

chapters.title: The Days After Counting
chapters.summary: Epilogue, September: Isandro's first college journal entry. He stopped counting days somewhere along the way. He writes to Theo every week. Beat: peace; the story of staying visible continues.
